query_text: Set up a new router for wifi access

messages.content: Set up a new router for wifi access

message.content:
To set up a new router for **Wi‑Fi access**, connect it to your modem, power the modem and router in the correct order, then use a browser to open the router setup page and finish the Wi‑Fi name/password settings.[1][3]

- Put the router in a **central, elevated, open location** away from thick walls, metal objects, microwaves, and other interference sources for better signal coverage.[1][5]
- Unplug your modem, connect an Ethernet cable from the modem to the router’s **WAN/Internet** port, then power on the modem first and wait about 2–3 minutes before powering on the router.[1][3]
- Connect a computer to the router with Ethernet if possible, or join the router’s default Wi‑Fi network using the SSID printed on the router.[1][2]
- Open a web browser and go to the router’s setup address, which is often **192.168.1.1** or **192.168.0.1**; TP-Link routers may also use **tplinkwifi.net**.[1][3]
- Log in with the default admin credentials from the router label or manual, then change the **administrator password** right away.[1][5]
- Follow the setup wizard to choose your internet connection type, enter any ISP username/password if required, and set your **Wi‑Fi name (SSID)** and **password**.[1][3]
- Update the router firmware if offered, and make sure basic security settings are enabled.[1][3]
- After setup, reconnect your devices to the new Wi‑Fi name and test internet access.[2][3]

If you want, I can also give you a **brand-specific setup guide** for TP-Link, Netgear, Asus, or Spectrum/Comcast-style internet service.
